A key word matches when it appears with no letter a to z and no digit 0 to 9 directly before or after it (other letters, such as ā, do not block a match). answers.rule: Under every question Helper asks, the person sees answers to pick, and can always type in the message box instead. An answer under a topic question carries the need id it gives (gives). Picking it shows that need's row at once: no key words, no model call. Under W1 the answers are the pick labels of the matched topics, or the labels of the matched terms, at most max_at_once of them in list order. Under F2, F3 and N1 the topic_picks are shown, in their order. A topic pick asks that topic's question if it was not asked yet in this visit and nothing is kept for it (keeps.use), else shows its row or plain line. A pick that holds two topics (topic_picks.holds) shows line C1 with those two topics to pick. There is no answer labelled none of these: the message box is that answer.

keeps.about: What Helper keeps, by fixed rules, with no asking. His words of 10 Nov, 19:00 (inputs/pb-words-10nov-keep-rules.md). Every rule here is followed by code. No model decides what is kept. The rules in plain words, the table of every question and answer, and the reasons: content/helper-keeps-v1.md.
keeps.tightened_19_15: His words of 10 Nov, 19:15 (inputs/pb-words-10nov-keep-little-skills-list.md): only what defines the person's Hermes setup, as little as possible, not always updating. So: what-you-do is used for the visit only and is not kept; at most 3 things on request; at most 7 kept things in all (name, mod, msg, svc, and 3 asked). A kept thing changes only when the person answers the same question again after Change, changes or deletes it on the settings page or the list, or tells Helper (remember that ..., forget my ...). Nothing is added from free typing. No model decides. Account: content/helper-keeps-v1.md.
keeps.depends_on_his_answer: Lead's reading, told to him and his to overrule: no model decides what is kept. Nothing a model returns is kept, except the name the model may fill at the opening (helper-talk-v2.md 2.1 step 3), which code checks.
rules: 1. From the opening: the name only. Written when the opening ends (F2, F3, or a name given with a question). What the person does is used for this visit and sent to their AI with this visit's messages; it is not kept (tightened 19:15).

2. From the conversation: an answer to one of the three questions in answers (mod-q, msg-q, svc-q), when the person picks it, or types it while that question is the open one and code finds it by the words listed here. A new answer replaces the old one.
3. On request: what follows a request start (remember.request_starts), word for word, within remember.limits.
4. Never: anything else the person types, anything a model returns beyond rule 1, anything that matches the K1 key patterns or remember.refuse.

5. Every kept thing has a use: a question is skipped, a line is chosen, or (the name only) it goes to the person's AI. Exception, changes-6: things kept on request (asked) have no use. They are kept and shown on the list, and nothing else. They are never sent to a model: hhtech ran one remembered sentence that turned 14 right answers into the memory line (docs/answers/hhtech-wants-check.md section 9). They stay because Pēteris asked for them.
6. Nothing is kept silently: every keep shows the grey kept line (tell) under Helper's line at that moment.
7. The way to see and delete everything kept ships in the same build that keeps anything: the list in the conversation (tell.see, typed). It needs no settings page.
8. At most 7 kept things in all: name, mod, msg, svc, and up to 3 asked. Each of the first four holds one value that is replaced, never added to.

9. Not always updating: a kept answer's question is not asked again, so it changes only through Change, through the list, or by telling Helper. Nothing is added from free typing except after a request start.

remember.rule: Step 1 b, straight after the key check and before the build words. Skipped while the memory question (mem-q) is the open one: there the message is the answer about Hermes. Lower-case the message and cut lead_ins from its start. If it then starts with a request start and has no question mark, it is a request to Helper. {thing} = the rest of the message as typed, without a leading that or colon. For the starts that end in i, i'm, im, my, we or our, {thing} begins at that word.

refuse.note: Also the K1 key patterns, which run first on every message. Everything kept is plain text on this computer and goes to the person's AI, so a secret must not be kept even on request.

facts.text: A model is the AI that does the thinking. Hermes needs one to answer.
The AI runs at a company you pay, or on your own computer.
You can switch to another AI at any time.

facts.text: Tools are actions Hermes can take, like searching the web or editing files.
A skill is a set of written steps that teach Hermes one task.
A plugin is an add-on that gives Hermes a new feature.

more.text: Hermes can do jobs on a schedule, such as a summary every morning.
MCP links Hermes to a service you already use, such as GitHub.

facts.text: You can chat with Hermes from apps like Telegram, WhatsApp or Slack.
It answers only while the computer running Hermes is on and awake.
For answers at any time, Hermes needs a computer that stays on.

facts.text: Each bot is a separate Hermes with its own settings and notes.
In the app, each bot has its own chat.
Each bot is a separate Hermes. They can hand work to each other with @ and a name.

where_line.text: In the Hermes app, "Bots" is the tab next to "Sessions", top left.
where_line.note: In place of a button: no call opens Hermes's own Bots tab (hhtech ran: 21 actions, none for Bots). Not the screen Profiles: it shows a word Helper never says and a folder path.

facts.text: Memory is short notes Hermes keeps about you and your work.
Hermes saves every chat. It can search your old chats when you ask.
Each bot keeps its own notes. For separate notes, use a separate bot.

build.model_hint: not a question: tells Helper or Hermes to make, write, install, set up or connect something for them
build.rule: Code turns it into line H1 with the paste box, as a build word does. Dropped when the message starts with a skip-start or has a how-phrase, and when code found exactly one topic by a full key word. Need must be empty.

model.strong_topic_final: hhtech's change A. When code found exactly one topic by a full key word or misspelling, the model cannot change that topic or turn it into none. Its need is used only when its topic is that same topic. Topics found by weak key words, a pending topic, and two or more matched topics stay open to the model.
